mismatch.error: UnsupportedHeroCommandBoundaryError: encumberMessage is not available for otyp 323

summary: The admitted by-description writing case successfully creates the specifically described scroll and merges it into the observed HAPAX LEGOMENON stack. C write.c:dowrite then calls hold_another_object. On the accepted-inventory branch, invent.c:hold_another_object updates inventory and calls pickup.c:encumber_msg. JS writeEnv supplies hooks:{}, so invent.js hold_another_object cannot call its existing encumberMessage hook and the command stops at the first post-write boundary. The missing behavior is caller wiring in writeEnv; the C encumbrance routine is already ported.

callers: apply.c:use_marker delegates marker application to write.c:dowrite.
write.c:dowrite successful by-description branch calls invent.c:hold_another_object for the newly created scroll.
invent.c:hold_another_object accepted-inventory branch calls pickup.c:encumber_msg after update_inventory().
findings: C write.c:dowrite lines 313-385 creates the selected scroll, observes it when writing by description, then calls hold_another_object at line 380.
C invent.c:hold_another_object lines 1288-1291 reaches encumber_msg only after the new object remains in inventory and inventory display is updated.

JS write.js imports encumber_msg but writeEnv currently returns { state, hooks: {} }; invent.js hold_another_object requires hooks.encumberMessage and awaits it at the same successful-inventory point.

JS pickup.js encumber_msg already implements the burden message and go.oldcap/status update used by C pickup.c:encumber_msg. Supplying that existing function in writeEnv preserves source order and adds no RNG call.
